clue.text: Enjoyable experience of a big swimmer from a previous era?

definitions.meaning: a really good time, a ball, great fun

definitions.text: a big swimmer from a previous era?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a whale (big swimmer) belonging to a past era

explanation.surface: A fond memory of a giant creature of the deep from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom word by word: a whale is the big swimmer, and 'of a time' places it in a bygone era.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having tremendous fun, so it names a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

clue.text: Female just on the scene, turning up with honoured companion

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters of the word are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: something just on the scene is new
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A woman newly arrived, appearing alongside a distinguished partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses NEW to WEN; CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wench is an old or jocular word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Shorten a span

parts.note: a bridge spans a gap, so a span is a bridge

explanation.surface: An instruction to reduce the length of a span.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wood used in model-making

indicators.note: the letters are used inside the run of text model-making, sitting across its middle

explanation.surface: Timber employed by a model maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a tree whose timber is a common wood.

clue.text: Sailor Henry's was a Spanish Catherine

definitions.meaning: the deck officer next below the captain on a merchant ship
Henry VIII's first wife was Catherine of Aragon, a Spanish princess

explanation.surface: A sailor's link to Henry VIII and his Spanish queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII, English king with six wives, married Catherine of Aragon first, so she was his first spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer ranking just below the captain is a sailor; read as two words it is Henry's initial spouse.

clue.text: A US lot losing heart unfortunately in Oklahoman city

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone awry, so these letters are put into a new arrangement
the word lot loses its central letter, its heart

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of Americans ending up in an Oklahoma town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes the O from LOT, leaving LT; 'unfortunately' rearranges A, US and LT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is the second-largest city in the US state of Oklahoma.

clue.text: Bloke receiving Communion finally in church

indicators.note: the word for a bloke receives a letter into its body

parts.note: a bloke is a man, addressed as mister

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Communion is taken

explanation.surface: A man taking Communion at the end of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts N, the last letter of Communion, inside MISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, such as York Minster.

clue.text: A knight with additional decoration somewhere in Northern Ireland

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
trim is decoration added to clothing or furniture

explanation.surface: A knight given extra adornment somewhere in Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county and town in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Hesitation about time of abstinence? Back down

indicators.note: turned about, the hesitation word is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of a speaker hesitating
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Pausing over whether to give something up for Lent, then giving way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back down' looks like a reversal instruction but it is the definition; the turning signal is 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to give way or soften a stance, which is backing down.

clue.text: Gloomy, having eaten hard fish

indicators.note: the gloomy word takes the hard letter inside it as if eating it

parts.note: gloomy means sad
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable after a tough fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like food fish.

clue.text: Any number in peculiar top hats and skimpy female attire

indicators.note: the number letter goes in among the rearranged headwear letters
peculiar means odd, so the letters of the hats are put into an odd new order

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Odd headgear paired with revealing women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges TOP HATS to HOTPATS, and 'in' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are very short, tight shorts for women, scanty clothing popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Joy has to keep quiet and languishes

indicators.note: the word has keeps the other letters inside it, holding them

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
to pine is to languish or waste away

explanation.surface: Delight must stay silent while it fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy and contentment are synonyms for a state of being glad.

clue.text: What sounds like common bird sound

indicators.note: the answer is said the same as a word meaning common

parts.note: something common or vulgar is cheap

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which noise an ordinary bird makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheep is the short high chirp of a young bird.

clue.text: Vehicle with nothing on? That's funny!

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A naked driver in a vehicle is a comic sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious vehicle has three letters, but a four-letter one is needed for the rest to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic drawing or animated film is meant to amuse, the thing described as funny.

clue.text: Old car not starting creates fury

indicators.note: the word for an old car loses its first letter, not starting

parts.note: banger is British slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car that won't start makes its owner furious.
explanation.walkthrough: A BANGER is British slang for a decrepit old car; 'not starting' drops its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is extreme rage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Manage to communicate, that's clear

definitions.meaning: to succeed in getting a message across to an audience
to clear an obstacle such as a fence, or to recover from a setback

explanation.surface: Succeeding in making yourself understood, so all is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both putting an idea across and surmounting a hurdle.

clue.text: Pair to perform at front of one church in rehearsal

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed at the front, ahead of the final ones

parts.note: to perform is to act
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A couple about to perform ahead of a church service, in a run-through.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a session of practice before a performance.

clue.text: Cloth seen in porch in Oxford

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the run of words porch in Oxford

explanation.surface: Fabric spotted in a doorway in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twill cotton fabric used for trousers.

clue.text: Boy comes to end of the big book

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name

indicators.note: the last letter of the word the is taken

explanation.surface: A lad finishes reading a hefty volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy volume.

clue.text: This writer has a set of religious books planned

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, me
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: The author owns a collection of scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past participle of mean, as in intended or planned.

clue.text: I? I love to eat

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed foodie's declaration of what they adore.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'I' is the definition: I is the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: In the periodic table the chemical symbol of this halogen element is the letter I.

clue.text: Pussy is crossing avenue — caution!

indicators.note: the cat word straddles the avenue abbreviation, which sits inside it

parts.note: pussy is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: A warning shouted as a cat wanders across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a warning or proviso, a caution.

clue.text: Hero in police department

definitions.meaning: Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A star detective in the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, the CID is the detective branch of a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid is a Spanish national hero; the initials also name the British detective branch.

clue.text: Insincere toad sadly thinking of no one else?

indicators.note: things gone sadly have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A two-faced, toad-like person who is selfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selfish and thoughtless gives no regard to other people's feelings.
